title: When the ballot audits power
news: American voters handed Congress to the opposition after a President who cast the election as a referendum on himself was seen as wielding unchecked power.
link: Elections are the final form of accountability: power that ignores citizens' everyday concerns, such as the cost of living, is answerable at the ballot box. The editorial's warning, that parties tied to a leader's cult inherit his liabilities, is a lesson in why institutions must rank above individuals.
question: "Accountability is the price of power in a democracy." Discuss with reference to the relationship between leaders and institutions.

title: Anticipate, but with care
news: CERT-In is testing an advanced AI model to find software flaws before attackers do, but only on small datasets, wary of exposing sensitive public data.
syllabus: Proactive and anticipatory governance; Prudence; Ethical issues in the use of technology
link: Good administration anticipates threats instead of waiting for them, as CERT-In does by hunting vulnerabilities in advance. Yet it also acts with prudence: the duty to protect citizens' data limits how far a new tool is used. Proactivity with caution is responsible governance.
question: "Proactive governance requires both foresight and prudence." Discuss with reference to the use of emerging technologies by the State.

src: IE p. 13 (Idea Exchange: Sjoerd Marijne & Savita Punia)
title: A team that owns its vision
news: After two poor years, the women's hockey team asked for coach Sjoerd Marijne's return; he rebuilt cohesion through shared ownership, and the team won Asian Games gold and an Olympic berth.
syllabus: Leadership; Team building and motivation; Emotional intelligence; Work culture
link: Leadership that shares the vision, invites players to speak up and lets them meet without the coach builds ownership; authority grows when it is shared.
question: "A leader's vision succeeds only when the team owns it." Discuss with examples from public service.
